summary: Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University (~1973–1978) and Leiden University (~1979–1987), where he held a post in 1999 and taught Thomas Zehnder and Arlo Griffiths.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~2011–2018), supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later took a teaching post at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1946–1951) and under George Roerich (~1957–1960), later holding posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–1974), and SOAS (attested 1995).

Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where he was supervised by Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme (~1960–1974) and Paris Nanterre University, serving as Professor from ~1974 to 1991 and teaching Katia Buffetrille.

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol (~1995–1999) under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under Richard Gombrich.
Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and was supervised by Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017).

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (attested 1995), studied at the University of London, and held posts at Leipzig University (attested 1995) and UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2013).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist. He studied at Dorpat, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Harvard, later holding posts at Peking University (~1922–1937) and as director of the Sino-Indian Institute (~1927–1937).
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Yves Sondaar.
Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1815–1827). He was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from ~1835 to 1854.

Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Balliol College and under Lakshman Joo. He held positions at Merton, Brasenose, and All Souls, serving as Lecturer and Professor at Oxford from ~1977 to 2015.

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Oakwood Friends School, Haverford College, and the University of Chicago (~1964–1973), and served as Professor of Religion and Religious Studies at George Washington University (~1968–2017).
Alfons Fürst (born 1961) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1982–1987) and held a post at the University of Münster (~2006).

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the Sapienza University of Rome under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi (~1937–1941) and continued there conducting postgraduate research from ~1941 to 1954.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) studied Buddhist and religious studies at UPenn, Andover Newton, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1957–1963). He held posts at Harvard, served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1986–1994), and was Emeritus Professor at Hawaii.

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford. In Lahore, he served as Honorary Librarian at Panjab University (~1902–1928), Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1936), and Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (~1928–1936).

Alfred Foucher (1865–1952) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist in Buddhist studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure in 1885, he held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1914) and the University of Paris (~1907–1936), teaching Étienne Lamotte.
